items.question: How did the model breakthrough at IOI and IMO change your thinking about pursuing reasoning research?
items.object: The IOI and IMO model breakthrough and pursuing reasoning research
items.answer: Last summer, Alex had this breakthrough in like IOI and IMO. You know, I used to be a participant in IOI. And then I was like, oh, that's crazy. You know, model can already win medals, gold medals. At that time, I was an assistant professor at UC Berkeley. But then I'm thinking maybe I should try to rethink my career. It seems like making the model smarter will maybe have some bigger impact on the world. And then I just kind of had a conversation with Alex back in last October. And then I got super excited about this thing. And eventually I just joined OpenAI.

items.question: How do you think AI reasoning models will change the work of theoretical researchers?
items.object: AI reasoning models as tools for theoretical research
items.answer: I have some mathematician friends and I have some friends in other fields. So I think the way I want to tell them is that I feel like some may be afraid that AI will replace them. AI will just replace mathematicians. But I think it's really about empowering every theoretical researcher. Because AI really has this advantage of knowing so many stuff and connections. Currently, it seems like the problem hard for a human may not be hard for AI. And that's a really great thing. We can use AI to solve those problems, get new ideas, and then we can digest them and make new discoveries, just like Hongxun said. So I think some of them get very excited about this. And of course, one thing is that currently it's only on math, but I believe that because it's a general reasoning model, all the at least theoretical researchers, they can benefit a lot from that. I think the dream world will be like everyone have some access to the top level reasoning ability. So other researchers can use them to discover whatever they want to discover. And then basically, OpenAI will accelerate science a lot, because you are empowering every scientist to accelerate the science worldwide. And then that's our mission.

The response envisions universal access to top-level reasoning ability through AI.

items.question: How do you figure out how much to trust an AI model?
items.object: Calibrating trust in an AI model
items.answer: I have this method of every time you double your trust on a model and see when it fails. And if it fails, you just go back. And you do this every month. Then you can quickly get to the point where you can maximally trust the model, but also not break your stuff.
quotes: I have this method of every time you double your trust on a model and see when it fails. And if it fails, you just go back. And you do this every month. Then you can quickly get to the point where you can maximally trust the model, but also not break your stuff.

rubrics.text: The response proposes testing an AI model’s trustworthiness by repeatedly doubling the level of trust placed in it.
The response recommends returning to the previous level of trust when an increase in trust in an AI model leads to failure.
